utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Ahmet Sehic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, please, can you state your full name, spelling both your first and last names.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Ahmet Sehic. A-h-m-e-t S-e-h-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Sehic, can you please tell us your date of birth and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: 12 April 1963, Gostovici, Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, can you tell the Trial Chamber how you were employed when the war started in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: I was a metal worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after the war started, sir, did you continue being a metalworker, or were you engaged in other types of employment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: When the war started, I was a platoon commander in a Territorial Defence company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where was this Territorial Defence company, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: In the place where I was born, in Borovnica in Gostovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, how long did you remain a platoon commander with the Territorial Defence company in Borovnica, Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Approximately six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the conclusion of that six-month period, sir, did you join any other military unit or formation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: After that I was a company commander. At first I was a platoon commander, then a company commander, and finally a battalion commander. At first it was Territorial Defence, and later, as a result of the reorganisation of the army, conditions were put in place for the establishment of battalions and brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall approximately when it was that you became a battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And of which battalion were you the commander?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: At first it was the 3rd Mountain -- Battalion of the 318th Mountain Brigade. And later on, as a result of the reorganisation, it was the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall approximately when it was that you became the commander of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1995, either in March or in April. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And for how long did you remain in the position of commander of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Up to the end of the war; i.e., up to the signing of the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What type of brigade, sir, was the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: It was a mountain brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Trial Chamber or tell the Trial Chamber the immediate command above the 328th Mountain Brigade during the time you were the 5th Battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The 35th Division of the army, of the ground forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, of which larger formation was the 35th Division of the army?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: It belonged to the 3rd Corps of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, as the battalion commander of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade, who was your immediate superior officer?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Major Fado Zukic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to move closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, could you please move a little closer to the microphone. The interpreters are having trouble hearing you. And perhaps if you can repeat the name of the 328th Mountain Brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Mujarif Fazlic [as interpreted] was the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps I need to clarify this because it appears from the record that there are two names, neither of which are necessarily reflected in the transcript. Can you please very clearly and into the microphones give us the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade during the time period you were the commander of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And possibly spell his name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Major F-u-a-d Z-i-l-k-i-c. Major Fuad Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during the time period, sir, that you were the 5th Battalion commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade, where was the brigade headquarters located?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: It was in the culture hall in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, where was the headquarters of the 5th Battalion, the battalion that you commanded, during the time period you held that position?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of my battalion was in the village called Marici, and the rear command post was in the village of Borovnica in Gostovici, i.e., in a hamlet called Sehic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, other than the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade, what other ABiH units, if any, were in the immediate vicinity of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: There was the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. Can we get the name of that hamlet again, please. They seem to give the witness's name as the name of the -- of the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yeah, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, the transcript again has it perhaps a slight error. The rear command post of your battalion, you said was in the village of Borovnica in Gostovici. And then you gave a more specific location in a hamlet. Which hamlet was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Sehic, S-e-h-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, that's the same name as your family name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: There is an "I" at the end, so it's S-e-h-i-c-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the hamlet is Sehici and your name is Sehic.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sehic, can you tell us, sir: This 4th Manoeuvre Battalion that you just indicated, where was the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion located at the time you were the commander of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The command of the battalion was in an outbuilding in the vicinity of the school, again in Gostovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, sir, so that we're clear, when you say the command of the battalion was in an outbuilding in the vicinity of the school, which battalion were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The 4th Manoeuvre Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us when you say "an outbuilding in the vicinity of the school," can you describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: This was a building where the teachers of the school resided. It was a residential building, an auxiliary building which was a residential building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How far is this building from the school in Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you were to come out of the back door of the school, can you describe what you would see at this location?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: In front of the school, there was a gym, a sports hall. And then to the left of the entrance was the courtyard that was normally used by the pupils of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where was this house, this build, this outbuilding?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, sir, to which unit -- well, let me -- let me ask you this first: Who was the commander of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion was Major Haris Catic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So whom did Major Catic report as commander of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe that he reported to the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, Mr. Sehic, what was the purpose of manoeuvre battalions?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Manoeuvre battalions were used for rapid interventions on defence lines. In case of major attacks, the troops of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion would intervene and help the units that were already on the defence lines. In case of offensive or operations to liberate a certain area, the manoeuvre battalion would also be used for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the 328th Mountain Brigade have such manoeuvre battalions?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, Mr. Sehic, which military operations, if any, the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade, that is, your battalion, engaged in during the course of 1995.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Some of the troops - maybe 30 - participated in Operation Spring 1995 and Farz 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, to the best of your recollection, when Operation Proljece [Realtime transcript read in error [omitted]] 1995 took place.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: In mid-June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Farz 1995, what time period was that operation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. For the interpreters, it's Proljece and Farz. Could you not translate that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How many men, sir, were in the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade during 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Between 500 and 600 troops with the logistics platoon, or the rear platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir, why it is that in your previous answer you indicated that 30 troops from your battalion participated in Operation Proljece 1995, in light of the fact that you've told us you had between five and six hundred troops.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The remainder of the troops - i.e., one company - was on its regular tasks on the defence lines, and they would only temporarily engage in moving the lines or taking up the lines reached. The 30 troops that I mentioned before were directly involved in the two operations, Proljece and Farz 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In what capacity were these 30 troops directly involved in the two operations Proljece and Farz 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The units that were engaged in offensives used the 30 soldiers to carry out the wounded, the fallen soldiers. Mostly for those purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Sehic, when you say "the units that were engaged in offensives used the 30 soldiers," what units are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The manoeuvre battalions and the El Mujahid Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll return to this subject a little bit later in your direct examination, but for now, sir, I'd like to turn your attention to September 1995. You told us earlier that Farz 1995 was at the beginning of September 1995. That's line 7 of page 93. And I'd like you to tell us, sir, where you were, you yourself, when Operation Farz 1995 commenced. Where were you physically located?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: At the command post in a hamlet called Marici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the date that Farz 1995 commenced?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: I believe it was on the 10th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate time that operation commenced on that day?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Early in the morning, around 4.00 or maybe between 4.00 and 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that point in time, sir, how many companies were in the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: There were three mountain companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the 10th of September, 1995, do you recall where each of those three mountain companies of the 5th Battalion, 328th Mountain Brigade were deployed?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Company was deployed on the defence line Podpaljenik, elevation 511, Malovan Greda, in front of the village of Kesten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps the transcript wasn't clear. The locations you've just mentioned, were those all held by the 2nd Company or was that all three companies in those locations?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: One company was -- was just a stand-by. I don't know whether it was the 1st or the 3rd. And I'm sure that the 2nd Company was on the defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "the defence line," that's the line that you told us about a few moments ago, Podpaljenik, elevation 511, Malovan Greda, in front of the village of Kesten.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did the 2nd Company of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade remain along that defence line?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Two or three days. I'm not sure. Usually the companies would change after 48 hours spent on the line. But that time around I believe that the company's time on the line was extended on to the third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. You told us, sir, that you were in the command post in Marici on 10 September 1995. How long did you remain at that location?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: With touring the line from time to time, I remained for a full 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, Mr. Sehic, where you were on the 11th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Also at the command post, in the village of Marici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 2nd Company, 5 Battalion, 328 Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Commander of the 2nd Company was Sogolj Ismet, Ismet Sogolj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, have any communications with Ismet Sogolj on the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what the subject matter of those communications were.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: The company commander had the task of informing me about all the events up at the front line, everything that went on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the information that he conveyed to you on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: A vital piece of information was that he or the assistant for security phoned up after 1300 hours or around 1300 hours to say that in the village of Kesten they had captured -- there were a large group of persons captured, about 50 Serb soldiers, in fact, and they requested that I supply a truck to transport them to a place determined for the collection of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you just indicated to us "the assistant for security," can you tell the Trial Chamber who that person was.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: My assistant for security was Mr. Izet Karahasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you received this phone call around 1300 hours on 11 September 1995, where was Mr. Izet Karahasanovic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: He was in the village of Kesten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What steps, if any, did you take after receiving this request to supply a truck to transport the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: As in my battalion I did not have any trucks, I asked the brigade commander, Mr. Zilkic, to supply me with a truck and I conveyed the message sent to me from the spot saying that there were 50 Serb soldiers who had been captured and that we needed a truck to transport them to a place which had been set aside for gathering up the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, where this place which had been set aside for gathering up the prisoners was located?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was in Zavidovici somewhere, near the division command. I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Sehic, what, if anything, Major Zilkic told you after you requested the truck?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: He ordered me to go to the location and that he would send a truck after me and that we should organise all that in a military fashion, transport the prisoners, and that in the meantime he would inform the superior command and the military police about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After receiving this order from Mr. Zilkic, what did you do, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: I went -- I set out to that place -- or rather, the village of Kesten, and half an hour later I arrived. I reached the place where the captured persons were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive in Kesten on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: At about 1330 hours, perhaps a little later. I'm not quite sure. But certainly after 1330 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say on lines 21, 22 "I reached the place where the captured persons were," can you tell the Trial Chamber precisely where the captured persons were?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Some of those captured were in some sort of facility and in front of the facility. There were more inside than there were outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What kind of facility is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was like a house or some sort of centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Upon your arrival about 1330 hours on 11 September 1995, how many soldiers of the 2nd Company, 5th Battalion, 328th Mountain Brigade were present in the village of Kesten in and around this house or centre?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Well, in the broader area around Kesten there was a whole company. Now, near the centre, or dom, there were about ten or so soldiers, perhaps less. Most of the military men were along the road, the communication line running from Kesten to Prokop, and it was their task to secure the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In September 1995 do you recall approximately how many men were in the 2nd Company of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: About 100 soldiers, military men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than the prisoners or detained persons and the soldiers from the 2nd Company of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade, did you see any other persons in the village of Kesten at the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that when you arrived, you saw some of the prisoners and that there were also around ten or so soldiers from the 2nd Company. Did you see anyone else in Kesten when you arrived there on 11 September 1995 at about 1300 -- 1330 hours?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: As we had just entered the hamlet that day, there were other soldiers there too. Now, whether they were from the manoeuvres battalion or from the El Mujahid Unit that happened to be passing by that way going in the direction of Bozici or Djurici, it's a road with quite a lot of traffic, comings and goings. Now, I don't know if that's the answer you were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you speak with anyone, sir, upon your arrival in Kesten on 11 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Kesten, I was informed by my deputy about everything that had happened. Muhamed Omerasevic [Realtime transcript read in error [omitted]], my deputy, was in Kesten before I arrived with the company commander and assistant for security. So he informed me of the situation, how many people had been captured. He told me that there were some 50 persons who had been captured and that they were having problems with the Arabs, who were trying to seize the captured persons. And this man prevented them in doing that and he had to cock his rifle at one point, pointing it at one of these foreign soldiers, these Arab soldiers or whatever [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a few follow-up questions. You said your deputy was in Kesten before you arrived, and the transcript did not catch his family name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise to my colleague Mr. Mundis, but the transcript didn't record part of the witness's answer. On page 99, line 22 he said "Arab soldiers." I don't know from what unit they were." That was not recorded in the transcript. Could the Prosecutor clear that up with the witness perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First I'm trying to clear up the name of the deputy who is reflected on line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The family name of your deputy, sir, it says "Muhamed" and then the transcript didn't catch that. Can you repeat the name of your deputy commander who was present.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Omerasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's also a bit unclear, sir, who it was that cocked his rifle pointing at the foreign soldiers. Who took that action?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: My deputy, in order to protect the Serb soldiers who had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, these people that you've described as Arabs, who were these people, if you know?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, because all these foreign soldiers who were there that day or during those days, for some it was said that they were the El Mujahid, some others were referred to as Arabs, and others, again, even had some specific clothing from those Arab countries. I'm not certain. At the beginning they said that they were the El Mujahid, but they had uniforms, those ones; whereas, the other ones that were there, at that point in time most of them did not have uniforms, so I don't know that -- whether they were soldiers from the El Mujahid Unit. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My -- my last question for today, Mr. Sehic, is: When you just told us "at the beginning they said that they were the El Mujahid," what do you mean by "at the beginning"? When did they say that they were the El Mujahid?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC
utterances.text: Well, the problem is, you see, with the name. All those foreigners we called "the Mujahedin." We referred to them as "the Mujahedin," all of them. Now, some people would say "El Mujahid." Others would say "Mujahid," others again said "the Arabs." But as far as we were concerned, they were the foreign soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Sir, unfortunately we have to stop for today, and unfortunately we are not going to be sitting tomorrow. So will you please come back here on Monday, the 5th of November, at 9.00 in the same courtroom. And let me just say that you have now been sworn to tell the truth and you are now in the process of giving evidence. Please do not discuss this case with anybody. Okay? Thank you very much. You may stand down for today. Come back on Monday, the 5th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
